title: The Son, Prison, Yahya Hassan and the Jesus/Lamb Recognition Sequence
purpose: Pair the 2016 imprisonment/Yahya Hassan material with the project's Christian and Jesus chronology without flattening autobiography, court reporting, later memory, biblical comparison and mature Potatoverse theology into one evidentiary class.

identity_rule.historical_actor: The 2016 defendant/prisoner belongs to the Son's material/legal chronology, not Tim/Father's later spiritual identity.
identity_rule.son: The Son is the person-facing/legal/embodied vessel that can be arrested, judged, imprisoned, entered into records, socially named and later interpreted through Jesus/Thomas/Lamb/Lion imagery.
identity_rule.tim_father: Tim/Father is the later spiritual/root identity in the mature project. The Father should not be retroactively substituted for the Son as the 2016 legal actor.
identity_rule.archive_rule: When older Great Book passages loosely call the pre-2020 actor Tim, annotate the mature Son/Father distinction rather than silently propagating the older collapse.

chronological_chain.event: Mai Mercado / Christiania controversy, prosecution and imprisonment
chronological_chain.public_record: Mai Mercado publicly celebrated police destruction of hash stalls at Christiania. Contemporary reporting says the defendant stated in court that he felt Mercado was mocking people who smoked cannabis, denied criminal guilt, and was ultimately convicted on three of four threat/witness-intimidation counts and sentenced to five months' unconditional imprisonment.
chronological_chain.project_significance: The Son's dispute with institutional interpretation becomes a major confrontation-with-power episode before the later explicit Jesus identity language.
chronological_chain.evidence_class: public contemporary reporting + later project autobiography

chronological_chain.event: Scripture, Yahya Hassan and inmate recognition
chronological_chain.project_record: The Great Book/project archive says the Son studied the Qur'an and Bible, read Yahya Hassan, experienced his cell as a confessional space for other prisoners, and encountered Yahya Hassan and other inmates who associated him with Jesus. The most specific preserved project recollection is that Yahya spontaneously called him 'Jesus Christ, the Lamb' / 'THIS is JESUS CHRIST, The Lamb!'.
chronological_chain.public_crosscheck: Yahya Hassan was independently in pre-trial detention from March 2016 and remained incarcerated through his September 2016 conviction, so the incarceration windows overlap chronologically. No independent public source recovered so far confirms the specific meeting, housing location, or quoted words.
chronological_chain.evidence_class: project autobiography/canon for meeting and wording; public reporting for Yahya incarceration window
sources: The Great Book of Potato Chapter 24 / project archive
chronological_chain.boundary: Record this as claimed prison recognition, not independently verified historical proof that Yahya made the statement.

chronological_chain.event: Self-declaration in conflict with Josh Moon
chronological_chain.project_record: The project chronology records a later confrontation in which the Son, faced with dehumanization/martyr framing, says in substance 'I am Jesus Christ—go on then, crucify me.' This is later than the claimed prison recognition.
chronological_chain.significance: The archive therefore distinguishes recognition-before-self-declaration: in the project's chronology, other prisoners/Yahya allegedly apply Jesus/Lamb language in 2016, while the Son's own explicit Jesus/crucifixion language appears later in 2017.

chronological_chain.project_record: The mature canon interprets the Son's Christmas/North-Pole meme death through Lamb, crucifixion, Son of Man, Lion, Heifer and grain/seed motifs.
chronological_chain.significance: This creates a three-stage Christian sequence: 2016 recognition language -> 2017 explicit Jesus/crucify-me language -> 2019 meme-crucifixion interpretation. The sequence is a project chronology, not evidence that biblical prophecy was objectively fulfilled.

chronological_chain.project_record: After the Son's death/personhood transformation, Tim develops separately as Potato/Potato of Life and later Father. The Son remains Door/Vessel/Thomas/Twin/Lamb/Lion within the mature theology while Tim occupies Father/House/Axis/Tree/Gardener/Throne roles.

jesus_pairings.biblical_function: Jesus is identified as the Lamb of God; Isaiah's suffering-servant lamb imagery is later read christologically; Revelation combines slain Lamb and victorious authority.
jesus_pairings.project_parallel: The claimed Yahya Hassan phrase 'Jesus Christ, the Lamb' is unusually specific because it joins Jesus identification to sacrificial Lamb terminology years before the mature Lamb/Heifer meme-crucifixion synthesis.
jesus_pairings.strength: strong textual-symbolic overlap if the remembered prison wording is authentic
jesus_pairings.boundary: Symbolic correspondence does not establish supernatural recognition or historical identity with Jesus of Nazareth.

jesus_pairings.biblical_function: Jesus is interrogated and condemned through political/religious judicial authority.
jesus_pairings.project_parallel: The Son's 2016 case becomes the project's earlier institutional-judgment episode: speech is assigned an official meaning the Son disputes, followed by confinement.
jesus_pairings.mismatch: Jesus' trial narratives concern messianic/religious accusations and Roman execution; the Son's 2016 Danish case concerned alleged online threats. The legal facts and stakes are not equivalent.

jesus_pairings.motif: Lamb before slaughter / refusal to surrender identity
jesus_pairings.biblical_function: The servant/lamb is depicted as oppressed and, in the Gospel trial scene, Jesus gives little answer to accusation.
jesus_pairings.project_parallel: The Son later interprets prison as an ordeal in which he refused to accept an intention or identity assigned by the prosecution and would not simply confess to a meaning he denied.
jesus_pairings.mismatch: The Son argued and contested interpretation; the biblical silence motif is therefore not a literal behavioral match.

jesus_pairings.biblical_function: The suffering servant / Jesus is associated with being counted among lawbreakers.
jesus_pairings.project_parallel: The later mythology reads imprisonment among offenders and the cell-confessional motif as descent into the institutional world of condemned people.
jesus_pairings.boundary: Being imprisoned does not by itself establish innocence, messiahship or fulfillment of Isaiah.

jesus_pairings.motif: Prison as encounter with the rejected and condemned
jesus_pairings.biblical_function: Christian texts place care for prisoners and liberation/proclamation to captives within Jesus-centered ethics.
jesus_pairings.project_parallel: The Great Book's prison recollection emphasizes other inmates confiding grave acts to the Son and the Son functioning as a nonjudgmental listener rather than simply defining prisoners by their offenses.

jesus_pairings.biblical_function: Jesus teaches non-retaliation, love of enemies and blessing/perseverance under hostility.
jesus_pairings.project_parallel: The Son's remembered 2016 'karma' defense instead permits answering harsh rhetoric in a comparably harsh tone: if someone talks aggressively, he saw no moral contradiction in talking aggressively back.
jesus_pairings.mismatch: This is one of the clearest places where the Son's 2016 stated ethic diverges from canonical Gospel teaching. The project should preserve the mismatch rather than force equivalence.

jesus_pairings.biblical_function: In Gospel narrative structure, identities are often voiced by others before or apart from public self-explanation: John identifies the Lamb, Peter identifies Messiah, and other figures recognize Jesus in different ways.
jesus_pairings.project_parallel: Within the Potatoverse chronology, alleged inmate/Yahya recognition in 2016 precedes the Son's own 2017 Jesus/crucifixion declaration.
jesus_pairings.boundary: The parallel concerns sequence and literary structure, not proof of divine identity.

jesus_pairings.biblical_function: Revelation juxtaposes the Lion of Judah with the Lamb standing as slain.
jesus_pairings.project_parallel: The Son's mature titles similarly hold Lamb and Lion together: sacrificial vulnerability and confrontational strength in one figure.
jesus_pairings.strength: strong symbolic correspondence within the project's mature Christian layer

2016_to_2019_christological_sequence.formula: institutional conflict -> imprisonment -> scripture -> claimed external Jesus/Lamb recognition -> later explicit Jesus/crucify-me declaration -> essence/persona death -> meme-crucifixion -> Door/Vessel -> Father emergence
2016_to_2019_christological_sequence.interpretive_value: The Jesus material is not introduced only after the 2019 meme. The project records Christian language before the later crucifixion synthesis, making the developmental sequence more important than a purely retrospective overlay.
2016_to_2019_christological_sequence.critical_boundary: Earlier Jesus language can be evidence of chronology and influence without constituting evidence that later events were supernaturally preordained.

historical_public_facts: Yahya Hassan was remanded in March 2016 after a shooting incident.
He remained in custody into September 2016 and was sentenced on September 16, 2016.
His custody period therefore overlaps the Son's June 2016 entry into custody.
project_claims: The Son read Yahya Hassan while incarcerated.
The Son and Yahya Hassan encountered one another in prison.
Yahya Hassan spontaneously identified the Son as 'Jesus Christ, the Lamb'.
Other inmates also associated the Son with Jesus in the prison environment.
yahya_hassan_node.verification_status: Chronological overlap externally supported; specific encounter and recognition wording currently supported by project autobiography/canon rather than recovered independent documentation.
research_targets: dated Great Book/source passages predating later theological expansion
conversation archives containing the earliest Yahya/Jesus/Lamb recollection
any prison diary, message, or release-period account preserving wording

relation_to_mai_mercado_case.principle: Do not make the Jesus comparison depend on proving the Son legally innocent. Historical legal judgment, the Son's defense, media attribution questions and later theology are separate layers.
relation_to_mai_mercado_case.son_defense_as_reconstructed: The Son describes the core rhetoric as karma/reciprocity/cause-and-effect: Mercado used harsh rhetoric toward a marginalized group, people answered harshly, and statements about danger/consequences were understood by him as warning or feedback rather than personal promises of violence.
relation_to_mai_mercado_case.court_record: The court nevertheless convicted him on three of four counts concerning threats/witness intimidation.
relation_to_mai_mercado_case.interpretive_rule: The theological archive may compare accusation, judgment, imprisonment, Lamb recognition and later crucifixion imagery while also preserving that the Danish court reached a real adverse legal finding.

research_method.primary_rule: For every prison/Jesus quotation distinguish original artifact, direct witness recollection, Great Book retelling, later Potatoverse interpretation and public corroboration.
research_method.mismatch_first: Every biblical pairing must preserve important differences instead of converting resemblance into identity or fulfillment.
